source_title: ‘The Pitt’ Star Jeff Kober Wins Daytime Emmy for ‘General Hospital’ After History-Making Nominations - People.com
source_excerpt:
The actor became the first performer to earn Primetime and Daytime Emmy nominations in the same calendar year
Jeff Kober won Outstanding Guest Performance in a Daytime Drama Series at the 2026 Daytime Emmys
The Pitt actor previously won a Daytime Emmy in 2022 for his portrayal of Cyrus Renault on General Hospital
Kober also earned a Primetime Emmy nomination this year for his work on The Pitt
Jeff Kober has another Daytime Emmy to add to his collection.
The Pitt star, 72, won Outstanding Guest Performance in a Daytime Drama Series for his portrayal of Cyrus Renault on General Hospital at the Daytime Emmy Awards on Friday, Oct. 30. He was not in attendance to accept the award.
Kober first joined the ABC soap in 2020 as the dangerous criminal whose arrival in Port Charles brought trouble for Sonny Corinthos and other residents. He returned to the series in a dream sequence in December 2025.
The actor previously won Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Drama Series for the role in 2022, following a nomination in the same category in 2021.
His latest victory comes after he made history as the first actor to earn both Primetime and Daytime Emmy nominations in the same calendar year, receiving the former for his role on The Pitt.
Kober beat out Jasmine Burke as June Hughes on Beyond the Gates , Eva LaRue as Natalia Rogers-Ramirez on General Hospital , Christopher Sean as Paul Narita on Days of Our Lives and Ray Wise as Ian Ward on The Young and the Restles s.
Burke earned her first Daytime Emmy nomination for her portrayal of June Hughes on Beyond the Gates , which premiered in February 2025. Her character, a woman experiencing homelessness, becomes embroiled in a legal battle before being revealed as the biological mother of Samantha and Tyrell Richardson.
In addition to acting, Burke is also a filmmaker, writer and producer whose credits include The Vampire Diaries , Army Wives and Saints and Sinners . This was her first Daytime Emmys nomination.
LaRue, 59, also earned a nomination for her work on General Hospital , where she played Natalia Rogers-Ramirez. The character was introduced in February 2024 as the mother of Blaze, played by Jacqueline Grace Lopez, and became involved in the drama surrounding her daughter’s relationship with Kristina Corinthos-Davis.
Natalia’s disapproval of the relationship created tension in the story, giving LaRue plenty of emotional material to explore during her run on the ABC soap. Her final episode aired in July 2025, following a storyline that brought her time in Port Charles to a dramatic close.
LaRue has a long history in television, having played Dr. Maria Santos on All My Children for years before starring as Natalia Boa Vista on CSI: Miami . She previously won a Daytime Emmy for Outstanding Guest Performer in 2020 for her role as Celeste Rosales on The Young and the Restless .
Sean, 41, was nominated for his portrayal of Paul Narita on Days of Our Lives . The actor joined the soap in 2014, playing the professional baseball player who later became involved in some of Salem’s biggest romantic and family storylines.
Outside of daytime television, Sean has appeared in projects including Hawaii Five-0 and the animated series Star Wars Resistance , in which he voiced Kazuda Xiono.
Wise, meanwhile, was recognized for his portrayal of Ian Ward on The Young and the Restless . The actor first appeared as the villainous cult leader in 2014 before returning to Genoa City in 2024.
The actor is a familiar face to television fans beyond daytime, with credits including Twin Peaks and Fresh Off the Boat . He previously won the Daytime Emmy for Outstanding Special Guest Performer in 2015 for playing Ian.
